gloss: to make sense; to be logical; to be consistent

definitions.gloss: to make sense; to be logical; to be consistent; to be coherent
definitions.explanation: For an argument, explanation, or course of action to follow a clear, logical thread from beginning to end.

examples.japanese: その{説明|せつめい}は{筋|すじ}が{通|とお}っている。
{筋|すじ}の{通|とお}った{意見|いけん}を{述|の}べてください。
{彼|かれ}の{主張|しゅちょう}は{最初|さいしょ}から{最後|さいご}まで{筋|すじ}が{通|とお}っていて、{反論|はんろん}のしようがなかった。
examples.english: His argument was consistent from start to finish, and there was no way to refute it.

notes:
{筋|すじ}が{通|とお}る uses {筋|すじ} in the sense of "logic" or "reasoning" (like a thread running through something) and {通|とお}る (to pass through). The image is of a logical thread running cleanly through an argument.

The negative form {筋|すじ}が{通|とお}らない means "to not make sense" or "to be illogical."

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {筋|すじ}が{通|とお}っている (makes sense — ている form is most common)
- {筋|すじ}の{通|とお}った〜 (a logical/coherent... — used as a modifier)
- {筋|すじ}が{通|とお}らない (doesn't make sense)

RELATED EXPRESSIONS:
- {筋|すじ}を{通|とお}す: to follow proper procedure, to do things the right way — the transitive counterpart
- {道理|どうり}にかなう: to be reasonable — more formal with similar meaning
